newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia says 12 firms eye energy selloff.
newsitem.headline: Latvia says 12 firms eye energy selloff.

text.p: The Latvian Privatisation Agency (LPA) said on Wednesday that it has completed talks with 12 investors interested in taking part in the sale of the Baltic state's monopoly energy provider, Latvenergo.
LPA director general Janis Naglis said that the 12 were all foreigners and included financial institutions and utilities.
"Now we know what the investors want and we are in the process of compiling a summary report," Naglis told a news conference.
The sale of Latvenergo will be one of the largest privatisations in Latvia.
The LPA is still thrashing out a deal for Latvian Gas with German firms Ruhrgas and Preussen, who want government guarantees for the debts run up by the company.
A new, postponed deadline of February 15 has been set for signing that deal.
Naglis said that the selloff of Latvenergo would not involve special conditions to attract Latvian firms.
"We are not going to build a protective bulwark against foreign investors," Naglis said.
He added that a new energy policy being drawn up by the government would make life easier for the potential privatisers as it would set out a strategy for the energy sector.
